title: Technology Sector Update for 04/27/2018: NXPI,QCOM,MSFT,INTC,FLEX

Technology stocks were slightly lower late Friday afternoon, giving back small gains earlier in the session and shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing nearly 0.2% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a nearly 0.8% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ NXP Semiconductors NV advanced over 3% on Friday after analysts at SunTrust today raised their investment rating for the chipmaker to Buy From Hold. Separately, prospective merger partner Qualcomm ( QCOM ) earlier Friday said it was extending its cash tender offer for NXP shares by another two weeks through the close of business on May 11. According to Qualcomm, investors owning about 43.6 million NXP shares - or about 12.7% of its outstanding stock - have accepted the Qualcomm buyout offer and have tendered their shares through Thursday night, down from nearly 55.9 million shares, or about 16.2% of outstanding NXP stock two weeks ago.
In other sector news:
+ Microsoft ( MSFT ) rose Friday after the software and hardware giant reported fiscal Q3 net income of $0.95 per share, rising 36% over year-ago levels and beat the Capital IQ consensus call by $0.10 per share. Revenue climbed 16% over the year-ago period to $26.8 billion, also surpassing the $25.7 billion Street call.
- Intel ( INTC ) was fractionally lower in Friday trading dispite reporting adjusted Q1 net income of $0.87 per share and blowing past the Capital IQ consensus expecting $0.72 per share. Revenue rose 13% over year-ago levels to $16.1 billion, also topping the $15.07 billion Street view. It also issued above-consensus Q2 guidance, prompting an upgrade for Intel shares at Bernstein to Market Perform from Underperform while RBC Capital IQ raised its price target by $4 to $58 a share.
- Flextronics International ( FLEX ) fell to a 20-month low on Friday after reporting fiscal Q4 net income lagging Wall Street estimates and providing below-consensus Q1 earnings guidance, also prompting a downgrade to Market Perform from Strong Buy by analysts at Raymond James. It earned $0.28 per share during the quarter ended March 31, trailing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue grew 9% year over year to $6.41 billion and topped the $6.27 billion analyst mean. It is projecting net income for the current quarter ending June 30 in a range of $0.22 to $0.26 per share on between $6.3 billion to $6.7 billion in revenue compared with the Street at $0.32 per share on $6.3 billion in revenue.
